newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts shake off early losses, end higher.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts shake off early losses, end higher.

text.p: UK gilts pulled back from their early Monday lows, ending a touch firmer on the day after slower than expected money supply growth helped the market higher.
"We started off with a bit of European-inspired weakness, but that encouraged a few of the more alert punters to put a bit of money into the market," said a salesman at a securities house in London.
He said talk of yield curve steepening characterised the market early in the session.
In the futures market, the June gilt contract ended the day 5/32 higher at 112-00 after plotting an early low at 111-16.

Data released at 0930 GMT showed M0 money supply growth slowed to 6.5 percent in February from a revised 7.3 percent in November. Those figures, coupled with the February Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), suggested moderate growth in the economy with no unduly worrying signs of inflationary pressure. The PMI fell to 53.5 in February from 53.9 in January. "The numbers today gave us no great clues -- although the money supply was marginally encouraging," said the salesman.
Analysts said the data lent weight to Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's bid to keep base rates at their present 6.0 percent until after the next election.
"This should be well received by the UK curve and provides the Chancellor with additional ammunition to justify a steady rate stance," said Jeremy Hawkins at Bank of America.

Looking ahead, traders said there would be little to kick start the market until Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gives the second part his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony before the U.S. House Banking Committee on Wednesday.
After Greenspan sent global bond markets scuttling for cover last week when he warned about inflation risks, analysts said any similar comments could spark a second bout of selling this week.

But gilts are set to hold up reasonably well in the face of any unpleasant surprises from across the water. "We are now back to a level against the core European markets where gilts look particularly attractive," said one trader. "So hopefully we could outperform if there is a sell-off."

The 10-year gilt/Bund spread stood at 180 basis points by the end of the session, having bloated from 173 at the start of Friday's session. At the short end, June short sterling futures ended the day 0.03 higher at 93.47. -- Kate Kelland, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2774 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
